{{Short description|Sensory evaluation tool}}
The '''Just-About-Right scale''' ('''JAR scale'''), is a [[sensory evaluation]] tool used to measure the intensity of a particular attribute or characteristic of a product or service. The JAR scale typically consists of 5 levels ranging from "Much too little" to "Much too much."<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Li |first1=Bangde |last2=Hayes |first2=John E. |last3=Ziegler |first3=Gregory R. |title=Just-about-right and ideal scaling provide similar insights into the influence of sensory attributes on liking |journal=Food Quality and Preference |date=October 2014 |volume=37 |pages=71–78 |doi=10.1016/j.foodqual.2014.04.019|pmc=4104712 }}</ref><ref name="Hare">{{cite journal |last1=Hare |first1=Lynne B |title=Statistics Spotlight: Caveat Emptor Measuring the effectiveness of a product or process requires proper test design and data analysis |journal=Quality Progress |date=August 2024 |volume=57 |issue=8 |pages=46–49 |url=https://asq.org/quality-progress/articles/statistics-spotlight-caveat-emptor?id=2edd7a2fd7b8445ea029a08aeb4fcf22 |access-date=9 September 2024}}</ref>

The JAR scale focuses on specific attributes of a product such as sweetness, saltiness, texture, etc., or service such as expediency, cost, etc.

The JAR scale is criticized for measuring attribute intensity and acceptability simultaneously.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Li |first1=Bangde |last2=Hayes |first2=John E. |last3=Ziegler |first3=Gregory R. |title=Just-about-right and ideal scaling provide similar insights into the influence of sensory attributes on liking |journal=Food Quality and Preference |date=October 2014 |volume=37 |pages=71–78 |doi=10.1016/j.foodqual.2014.04.019|pmc=4104712 }}</ref>
